title: How much does a PIM cost? License plus implementation
summary: PIM implementation runs about $30,000-$150,000 mid-market, often 50-200% of first-year licence, on top of licences from free to $300,000+ a year.
body_markdown:
A PIM implementation typically costs $0 to $5,000 for an entry-level tool and $30,000 to $150,000 for a mid-market project, or roughly 50% to 200% of the first-year licence, on top of annual licences that run from free to $300,000 or more ([Hootcore's cost breakdown](https://hootcore.io/blog/how-much-does-a-pim-system-cost) ). Those quotes pay for configuration, integrations, and moving your existing data, but rarely for creating the missing attribute values, and on a large catalog that work can cost more than the software.


## How much a PIM implementation costs, by scope tier


Published ranges cluster by catalog size and channel count. Hootcore's bands are a reasonable starting frame:


- **Entry:** under 10,000 SKUs and one to three channels. Licence from $0 to about $8,400 a year, implementation $0 to $5,000, mostly self-serve.
- **Mid-market:** 10,000 to 100,000 SKUs and three to eight channels. Licence about $25,000 to $60,000 a year, implementation $30,000 to $150,000.
- **Enterprise:** 100,000+ SKUs, often multi-country. Licence $75,000 to $300,000+ a year.


UK figures from[Bluestone PIM](https://www.bluestonepim.com/blog/pim-pricing-total-cost-of-ownership-guide) land in the same shape: free to £10k a year under 10,000 SKUs, £10k to £50k+ for 10,000 to 100,000 SKUs, and £50k to £100k+ above that. Polish integrator[Macopedia](https://macopedia.com/en/services/pim-systems/pim-academy/how-much-does-a-pim-implementation-cost) quotes PLN 50,000 to 150,000 for a basic implementation with no integrations and PLN 300,000+ once data import, multiple integrations, and training are in scope.


Timelines move cost more than anything else, because most of the bill is people.[Sitation's implementation guide](https://www.sitation.com/guides/pim-implementation-guide/) says there is no standard duration and cites one Akeneo rollout finished in 12 weeks and one Salsify launch, connected to JD Edwards, Bynder and SAP Commerce, in four months.


## What PIM software costs per year: published prices and reported contracts


Few PIM vendors publish list prices. Here is what the primary and transaction-data sources actually show.


**Pimcore** publishes its prices. The[Pimcore pricing page](https://pimcore.com/en/pricing) lists a free Community Edition, Professional at $9,900 per year and Enterprise at $29,900 per year (Professional on-premises, Enterprise on-premises or private cloud), and a managed PaaS edition on custom pricing. Self-hosting means your hosting and developer time sit outside that number.


**Akeneo** quotes by request.[Hootcore](https://hootcore.io/blog/how-much-does-a-pim-system-cost) cites a G2 listing at about $45,000 a year, a figure Akeneo does not publish itself, and notes separate charges for AI and connectors.


**Salsify** is also quote-based. Purchase data on[Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/salsify) shows a median contract of $52,100 a year, with reported deals ranging from $21,467 to $86,250.


Two pricing mechanics to watch. First, many tools price on SKU count, channels, locales, or modules, so the same platform can double in cost when you add a marketplace or a second language. Second, for on-premises licences,[Plytix](https://www.plytix.com/blog/pim-software-pricing/) notes that updates and support can run 15% to 25% of the licence fee per year. If you are still building a shortlist, our[ranked PIM software comparison](https://www.anglera.com/best/pim-software) and[guide to choosing a PIM](https://www.anglera.com/guides/how-to-choose-a-pim) cover fit before price.


## What the implementation quote covers: consulting hours, integration, migration


An implementation statement of work usually breaks into phases that[Sitation](https://www.sitation.com/guides/pim-implementation-guide/) describes as discover, design, build and migrate, then launch and adopt. Mapped to line items:


- **Data model and workflow design.** Families, attribute groups, validation rules, approval steps. Partner consulting hours.
- **Integrations.** ERP in, ecommerce and marketplaces out, maybe a DAM.[Plytix](https://www.plytix.com/blog/pim-software-pricing/) puts custom integrations at $3,000 to $20,000+ each.[Macopedia](https://macopedia.com/en/services/pim-systems/pim-academy/how-much-does-a-pim-implementation-cost) calls integrations the biggest single cost driver, mostly because of how many transformations the data needs between systems.
- **Data migration.** Plytix lists migration and cleanup at $5,000 to $30,000+, more if your data is messy.[Bluestone](https://www.bluestonepim.com/blog/pim-pricing-total-cost-of-ownership-guide) says migration, onboarding, configuration, and first integrations typically add 20% to 40% to an enterprise first-year budget.
- **Training and change.** Bluestone suggests budgeting at least 10% to 15% of first-year PIM spend.


Read the migration line carefully. Migration moves the values you have into the new data model. It maps` ERP_DESC_2` to` short_description` and splits a concatenated` Size/Color` field. It does not go find the` voltage` ,` IP_rating` ,` thread_size` , or` material` values that were never in your ERP to begin with.


## The line item nobody quotes: getting the data worth storing


A PIM is a well-organised container. When it goes live, the attribute schema for a category like cordless drills might have 30 fields, and your ERP export fills six of them: SKU, MPN, brand, a truncated description, price, and weight. Sitation calls data migration and clean-up often underestimated and often the largest variable, and lists moving unclean data into the new system and having no owner after launch as common mistakes. We wrote about why that gap persists in[your PIM stores the data, but the work remains](https://www.anglera.com/blog/pim-stores-data-work-remains) .


That gap gets filled one of four ways: your own merchandising team, an offshore data-entry vendor, a generic AI writing tool, or an enrichment layer that pulls values from spec sheets, manufacturer sites, and catalogs. The cost driver is the same in every case, which is minutes per SKU multiplied by SKU count, plus the new SKUs that arrive every month. AI buttons inside PIMs help with copy, but they generate text from what is already in the record. They do not source a missing` amperage` value. More on that in[your PIM added an AI button](https://www.anglera.com/blog/your-pim-added-an-ai-button) .

## Three-year total cost of ownership, illustrated


[Hootcore's TCO method](https://hootcore.io/blog/how-much-does-a-pim-system-cost) is sound: add three years of licence and support to one-time implementation, migration, integration, customisation, and training, then add three years of internal staff time, which it says frequently exceeds 20% of the total. Here is that method applied to a hypothetical distributor. Every input is an assumption chosen from the ranges above, not a benchmark.


Assumptions: 40,000 SKUs, of which 20,000 need meaningful attribute work; 15 minutes per SKU to research and enter missing values; $35 per hour loaded labour; 4,000 new SKUs a year; a mid-market licence of $50,000 a year; implementation at 100% of first-year licence; two integrations at $15,000 each; training at 10% of first-year spend.


Line item Basis Three-year cost


Licence $50,000 x 3 years $150,000


Implementation partner 100% of year-one licence $50,000


Integrations ERP in, ecommerce out, $15,000 each $30,000


Training and change 10% of $130,000 year-one spend $13,000


Initial attribute backfill 20,000 SKUs x 15 min = 5,000 hrs x $35 $175,000


New-SKU enrichment 4,000 SKUs x 15 min = 1,000 hrs x $35 x 3 $105,000


**Total** **$523,000**


In this illustration the two data lines come to $280,000, more than half the three-year total, and neither typically appears on a vendor quote or a partner SOW. Change the assumptions and the share moves: at 5 minutes per SKU the data lines drop to about $93,000. The point is to put the line in the budget, then decide who does it.


## How to get a PIM quote that matches reality


Before you sign, get these numbers in writing or work them out yourself:


1. **Licence escalators.** Price at today's SKU count, channels, and locales, and again at your three-year plan.
2. **What migration means in the SOW.** Mapping and loading existing values, or creating missing ones? Usually the former.
3. **[Attribute fill rate](https://www.anglera.com/glossary/attribute-fill-rate) today.** Export one category, count populated required attributes against the schema, and multiply the gap by a realistic minutes-per-value figure.
4. **Ongoing ownership.** Who enriches the 300 SKUs that arrive next month, and from which sources?


A PIM licence and implementation are predictable once you scope them. The data inside is the variable, and it is the part that decides whether the investment pays off. Anglera sits next to whichever PIM you choose and does that work from source documents, so you can budget for it as a maintained practice rather than discovering it after go-live.
